value.rationale: The natural inverse-digitization question asks where the unknown random disk center lies after observing the first full-dimensional (triangle) or all-four (square) lattice hull. Conditional spatial information is qualitatively absent from known marginal hull-area laws: a parabolic cap requires distinct square-root and linear scales, whereas a simplex requires two linear scales. Exact nonzero optimal total-variation coefficients quantify how accurately critical conditioning can be approximated, and distinguish exact triangle coverage from at-least-three coverage. This is a motivated two-scale localization classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice; the elementary nature of the underlying geometry is expressly recognized.
